ops.body:
Found and fixed 2026-08-29 while closing out the daemonkit v0.23.0 state-root migration. Fixed in `af2dbf5`, with a follow-up comment in `7fb4139`.

## The gap

`cc-skills` is a genuine daemonkit consumer — module `github.com/yasyf/cc-skills/plugins/codex`, shipping the `codex-ask` Homebrew cask — and the fleet-build gate had **never built it**. It was absent from `.github/workflows/fleet-build.yml`'s matrix and from `ci/fleet-refs.txt`.

That absence was **structural, not an oversight**. `checkout_of` resolved a module to `$src_dir/${module##*/}` — the module *basename* — so `cc-skills`' module resolved to `$src_dir/codex`, a directory that does not exist. Every `go.mod` read (`go_directive`, `fleet_requires`, `module_of`, `pinned_daemonkit`, `snapshot_manifest`, `restore_manifest`) and the build's own `cd "$source_dir"` all assumed the module sat at the checkout root. Adding a matrix line would not have worked; the script could not express the consumer.

## Why it mattered

The gate's stated purpose is that "a breaking surface change goes red BEFORE a release exists", and `ci/fleet-refs.txt` refuses a file that leaves any consumer undeclared, "because an omitted leg silently builds a branch nobody chose". Both guarantees were sound — and both were scoped to a consumer set that could not include cc-skills.

The visible consequence: cc-skills sat on **daemonkit v0.21.4** while all thirteen other consumers moved to v0.22.0 and then v0.23.0. It missed *both* state-root moves. Nothing reported it, because the only mechanism that would have was the gate that structurally excluded it. See [[a-daemonkit-consumer-migrates-when-it-ships-not-when-its-main-is-bumped]] for why an unbuilt consumer also stays unmigrated on every host.

## The grammar, and why not the obvious one

`ci/fleet-refs.txt` is now `<repo>[:<module-dir>] <ref> [goos[,goos]...]`, e.g. `cc-skills:plugins/codex  main`.

A bare fourth column was rejected: column three (the GOOS set) is optional, so a three-field line is ambiguous between `<repo> <ref> <goos>` and `<repo> <ref> <module-dir>`, and `check_refs` could not distinguish malformed from well-formed. A mandatory third column defaulting to `.` would rewrite all thirteen existing lines for one consumer and kill the optional-GOOS shape the header documents.

The colon form wins on a real property rather than taste: `<repo>:<module-dir>` **is exactly the module path minus the `github.com/<owner>/` prefix**, so the mapping is derivable in both directions instead of guessed. `checkout_of` now resolves by prefix strip and still requires the `go.mod` found there to declare that exact module — which reaches *into* the subdirectory rather than stopping at the repository, a strictly stronger identity check than the basename strip it replaces. `:` cannot appear in a GitHub repo name or a GOOS value, and everything that addresses a leg by name (`--only`, `--ref`, `--cone`, a cone peer, `matrix.repo`, `actions/checkout`'s `path`) still takes the bare repo, so the workflow needed only a matrix entry and a widened `cache-dependency-path` glob.

## What the adversarial review then found — the more important half

Two independent review passes (finder and refuter) over the change surfaced **six defects**, three of them false greens in a release gate:

1. **Data loss via relative `FLEET_SRC`.** `snapshot_manifest` embedded the uncanonicalized checkout path under `$work/orig`, so `FLEET_SRC=../../../..` normalized the backup target *outside* `$work` and overwrote an unrelated file — which the `EXIT` trap, scoped to `fleet-build.*`, then left behind. This violated the script's own explicit promise to leave every overlaid checkout byte-identical.
2. `cc-skills:.` passed validation and silently selected the root module, skipping the nested one.
3. `module_dir`/`repo_of` emitted data with `echo`, so a module dir of `-n` was consumed as an option.
4. **A zero-package module reported PASS**, because `go build ./...` exits 0 when `./...` matches nothing. A consumer that lost all its Go files, or excluded them under a build tag, would have reported `1/1 built`.
5. **A comma-only GOOS set ran no build at all** and kept `verdict=PASS` — the loop over `${goos_set//,/ }` simply had zero iterations.
6. `repo_of` projected every module under a repository onto that repository's single declared module, so a sibling nested module would be reported as overlaid while resolving from its published version.

**Provenance, established by replay rather than inferred from the diff** — each finding was re-run against the pure pre-change script at `f4fd007`, using `synckit` to build the same shape where that script has no vocabulary for cc-skills:

| # | Verdict | Evidence at `f4fd007` |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **introduced** | The sentinel survives — `snapshot_manifest` keyed on `basename "$dir"`, so `../../../../synckit` collapsed to `synckit` and the copy stayed inside `$work/orig`. |
| 2 | introduced | The colon grammar did not exist; `synckit:.` is refused as declaring a non-consumer. |
| 3 | introduced | `module_dir` and `repo_of` are new functions — no emitter existed to swallow a dash. |
| 4 | **pre-existing** | A `synckit` holding only a `go.mod` reports `PASS` / `1/1 built, 0 failed`. |
| 5 | **pre-existing** | `synckit main ,` reports `PASS` over a `synckit` that does not compile. |
| 6 | introduced | `--cone synckit` printed nothing; the old `${required##*/}` yielded `shared`, no fleet repo, so it dropped out. |

So **four introduced, two pre-existing** — and the data-loss blocker is one of the four. An earlier draft of this note said most were pre-existing, including #1; that was wrong, and the correction matters in a specific way: the change that *caused* #1 was itself right. Keying the manifest backup on the module directory's whole path instead of its basename is what stops two repos' `plugins/codex` restoring over each other. The basename was **masking** an unresolved `src_dir`; removing the mask exposed a latent defect rather than creating one. Canonicalizing `src_dir` is the real fix, and reverting to a basename key would trade a visible bug for a silent one.

**The lesson worth carrying:** a gate's own correctness is not covered by the gate. Three of these six made the script report success while measuring nothing, and none would ever have gone red to announce itself. A release gate earns an adversarial pass of its own — and specifically a **mutation check**: prove the leg goes red when the thing it guards actually breaks, not merely that it goes green when everything is fine.

## The verification shape that settled it

Per finding, a green→red→green bracket against the *reviewed* code. That code is preserved verbatim as `gate-repro/reviewed-fleet-build.sh` beside the report, with `rebuild-prefix.sh` materializing `af2dbf5`'s tree with it swapped in — verified two ways: it places all nine reviewer-cited line numbers on the statements they cited (126, 141, 152, 165, 194, 300, 337, 379, 383), and a cold rebuild reproduces `before.txt` exactly. (The harness had to move its scratch out of `$TMPDIR`: finding 1's escape resolves *relative to* the temp tree, so a synthetic tree pitched inside `$TMPDIR` changes where the pre-fix script's `..` segments land and stops reproducing the reviewed behaviour.)

For the gate as a whole: renaming `daemonkit.Stable` makes the cc-skills leg FAIL with `./daemon_runtime.go:17:28: undefined: daemonkit.Stable` against cc-skills' *own* source file — proving the leg compiles the consumer rather than no-opping, and ruling out a daemonkit self-build failure — and restoring it makes the leg PASS.

For regression safety: full fleet 14/14 against a baseline run of the unmodified script at 13/13, whose only textual difference is the leg count; every shared leg's verdict, `*` mark, ref, pin, path and cone list byte-identical. CI on `af2dbf5` then re-ran the whole matrix on the real runner — all six workflows green, `fleet-build (cc-skills)` among them.

**One limit, stated plainly:** finding 3's fix is proven at the resolution layer only. A leg whose module directory begins with a dash still does not build, because the Go tool itself refuses it (`invalid input directory name "-n"`). That is Go's constraint, not the gate's, and `--cone` is the bracket that isolates the emitter.
